🌡️ Language models

Temperature

In simple words

A setting that controls how predictable or surprising a language model's choice of words is.

A setting that changes how a language model picks the next token. At a low temperature it almost always takes the most likely token, so its answers are predictable and repeat themselves. At a higher temperature less likely tokens get more of a chance, so answers are more varied and surprising, but also more often odd or wrong.

Example. Ask for the start of a story at a low temperature and you'll get almost the same one every time. Turn it up and every story is different; at very high values the sentences stop making sense.

Related words

  • Next-token predictionWhat a language model does: it gives every possible next token a probability, picks one, and repeats.
  • HallucinationWhen an AI confidently gives an answer that sounds right but is false or made up.
